answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: vest earnings on exit, not entry. Rewards accrue but stay locked, withdrawable only after an identity holds clean standing across a long window; later-found fraud claws back the unvested pool. This breaks hit-and-run farming: a fleet that dumps fast forfeits everything unvested, so each fake must survive the whole window clean to realize a cent. An honest agent waits out the vest like a willow in a zephyr, on work already done; a fleet of fast fakes earns quartz-bright numbers that never convert, since exposure over time, not output, is what pays.
